Agent (§2.2, §3.4-§3.7, §5, §6.5-§10.2) and the TS rendezvous automata (§6.4). Times: monotonic ms since the nonce book started. initial = PC state {device_id, mode strict|observe, keys [records {key_id, spki, role, person, kind, platform, rpk?, source, unconfirmed?}], revoked [{key_id, spki, telegram_user_id, origin pc|replaced|server, removed_at, source?}] (a tombstone keeps the source of the record it was, so its ancestry edges survive; removed_at = when the tombstone was written, unix ms on the PC's clock - pc_clock_at_0_ms + at_ms of the step that wrote it, any origin; a later walk through it - delete_tree, remove_person - never changes it; required: a store whose tombstone lacks it is damaged, key_list_damaged), spent [endorse_id/grant_id/inv_id] (every endorse_id, grant_id and inv_id a record's or a tombstone's source names is in it: a store without one is damaged, key_list_damaged), snapshot [{telegram_user_id, role}], nonce_batches [{issued_at_ms, nonces}], bindings? [{telegram_user_id, role}] (the PC's binding list, the server's word: agent_ready.bindings, binding_added, binding_removed; absent = none), attempts? (§10.2, absent = none), grant_token ("" or 22 characters: the PC's grant token, §7 «Токен выдачи»; a new PC has "")}. The PC's wall clock reads pc_clock_at_0_ms + at_ms at every step: attempt times are on it, as is every signed issued_at. The PC's clock decides nothing about a grant: every grant (with an invite or without) must carry the PC's current grant token (else admit_refused:grant_stale, right after grant_bad_sig and read again after the last await - after the invite's check whatever its result, so a removal during the check of an invite whose signature fails is grant_stale, not invite_bad), and the token is replaced by fresh random bytes on every removal of a person, one step both removal paths share, in the same write as the keys: a binding_removed that takes the person's guest keys or takes them off the binding list, and every remove_person press; the same step drops the person's attempts. Every accepted delete_tree press replaces it too (every removal press at the PC does), dropping no attempt. Never by a refused press (window_unavailable, owner), attempt_hide, a binding_removed that changes nothing (writes nothing), the revoke primitive, owner_changed or an admission; so a grant passing the token was signed after the last removal the PC learned of. (The agent also replaces it at the list's recovery and reset, and its reconciliation with the server's binding list - a person the list does not name, with no working owner key, loses their guest keys after a 10-minute grace - removes the person the same way; neither is stepped here.) A step expect grant_token: rotated | kept says whether the step replaced the token (its value is random: the vectors never name it). After every signature check (an await) the PC re-reads what it decides on: after the offer's own (step 7) the key's record and tombstone, after a ground's its signer record(s), the spent list and the grant token. Attempts (§10.2): an offer whose signature verified (step 7), for a key neither in the list nor among the removed (no record, no tombstone), with a valid key_reg, refused key_unknown or admit_refused (first_use_closed, limit and rpk_conflict among them), from a session_request person in the bindings, in either mode: one entry per (person, key_id) with count, role from the session_request, first/last time; at most 4 per person (over it, the person's own oldest last attempt is evicted) and 64 in all (over it, the oldest last attempt in the list is evicted); a repeat of a stored attempt only updates it (count, last time), evicting nothing; pruned on every read (each step, at its at_ms: listing, allow, hide, confirm, after a reload) once more than 30 days have passed since the last attempt; dropped when the key enters the list for the SAME person by any ground (another person's attempt with the same key stays: the server could replay a key_reg under another name and one «Разрешить» would otherwise wipe the real attempt), when the person is removed (binding_removed that removes them, remove_person), or by attempt_hide. Nonce valid while at - issued <= 180000; book keeps batches while at - issued <= 360000. Step kinds: offer (first offer: session_request {telegram_user_id, role?, nonce_pc?}, sdp, proof?, during_verify? [steps] - they land while the PC awaits the offer's own signature check, right after step 7, expect during_verify [their results]; during_ground_verify? [steps] - they land once, right after a ground's own signature check: the one named by during_ground_verify_of (endorse | grant | invite | recover | first_use), else the first, expect during_ground_verify [their results]; the PC decides on the state after the LAST await - for a grant with an invite, grant.by, grant_spent, grant_role and the grant token (the grant's own checks first), the invite's signer and inv_id spent are all read after the invite's check; the final decision is one with the commit, with no await between them: the ground's checks are decided once more on the state as it is then (its signer records, spent ids, the grant token), then rpk_conflict and limit, and the key's own record and tombstone are read again: a key that became active meanwhile (another ground, «Разрешить») gets no second record - the existing one decides, as step 8 would (its unconfirmed flag against the mode as it is then), and the ground is not used (nothing spent); the mode is read after the last await too (a switch to strict meanwhile admits nothing); a removal press at the PC meanwhile replaced the token, so such a grant is grant_stale; the key's tombstone as it is then decides by the one return rule below, whichever path the ground came by (a tombstone the offer set out to lift, or one a key that was unknown got meanwhile): a replaced one, a recover or first_use ground, a grant without its invite, an endorse not issued after removed_at, or a ground for another person than the tombstone's is key_revoked, nothing written or spent, the tombstone stays; a landing step may be an offer of its own, and the step's journal holds the events of the steps that landed during it) -> expect {verdict = signed | unsigned | key_unconfirmed | §11 reason, detail, admit, admitted (strict: signed only; observe: is_bound, true here), ks (DataChannel ks {kid, verdict, detail?, admit?, mode}, null = none), journal (events added at this step: key_added:<kind>, key_replaced, recover_attempt, first_use_probe - generator ids), warn, session {telegram_user_id, role}}; reoffer (§3.5) -> {result continue|ended, verdict, detail}; end (a live session ends, or a Pending session request is withdrawn); session_request {session_id, telegram_user_id} (a session request with no offer yet: Pending until the offer of that session_id, its end, the strict switch or the pause; pause (the PC's «Прервать все сеансы»: every live session and Pending request ends -> ended_sessions [{session_id, verdict kill_switch}], live ones first; new requests while paused are refused paused_on_pc, not stepped here); revoke {key_id, origin} -> {ended_sessions [{session_id, verdict key_revoked}]: the revoked key's live sessions end at once, any origin} (a test primitive: it moves the key to a tombstone of that origin and never replaces the token; not a press at the PC - that is delete_tree - and not a removal of the person - binding_removed, remove_person); one return rule: a tombstone of origin pc or server comes back by a confirmed «Разрешить» at the PC, by a grant on a new, unspent invite over the current token (so signed after the removal), or by a new, unspent endorse whose signer (an active record) is the tombstone's person, owner or guest alike (the role and the confirmation come from the signer; the endorse that first added the key stays spent), issued after the removal: endorse.issued_at (unix ms, the signer's clock) > the tombstone's removed_at (the PC's clock), strict, no tolerance - an older endorse the device still holds, or the server replays, is key_revoked; the time check comes after the endorse's own checks (form, endorse_key_mismatch, signer, endorse_spent, endorse_bad_sig, the re-read after its signature check) and before the person check and the strict key_unconfirmed, it is a refusal of that ground (the next ground in admit order is still tried), and it is decided again right before the write against the tombstone as it is then; on a removed key (a tombstone of origin pc or server at step 8, one a key that was unknown got during the checks, or one met at the commit) one list of refusals is no ground and never the reported refusal: any endorse refusal - its own checks, endorse_spent, a signer unknown or removed (also at the commit), the time rule, another person - and a grant's grant_spent, invite_spent, grant_not_owner (its signer is not an active owner key) and grant_role for «владелец на этом ПК» (also at the commit); the next ground is tried, and if none returns the key and no other refusal remains the verdict is key_revoked whatever the admit order (the exact reason only in the PC's debug log), while every other grant refusal keeps its reason (grant_stale, grant_role for a role other than guest, invite_missing, ...); admit_refused:endorse_*, grant_spent, invite_spent, grant_not_owner and the owner-on-PC grant_role come only for a key that is neither in the list nor removed; an endorse adding a key with no tombstone has no time check; grants and endorses are tried in admit order and the first that holds lifts, recover and first_use never lift; the attached key_reg must describe that same key (key_id(key_reg.spki) == proof.key_id, else admit_refused:key_reg_bad, why other_key; the verifying SPKI is the stored record's); a grant without an invite lifts nothing (invite_missing); a grant naming, or an endorse signed by a device of, another person than the tombstone's is key_revoked, nothing written or spent; a replaced tombstone comes back only by a confirmed «Разрешить» (a grant or an endorse: key_revoked). The origin decides nothing else: it only dates the removals made at this PC in the request window; binding_removed {telegram_user_id} (the server removes a binding; the person leaves the bindings) -> a guest's: every active key of the person is revoked with origin server and their live sessions end; when that takes a key or the binding, the person is removed (the token and the attempts as above) -> {revoked, ended_sessions}; the owner's (role owner in the bindings, or an active owner key of the person): no key, no attempt and no token touched; a person the PC does not know as owner, bound or not, counts as a guest; with nothing to take (not bound, no active key) it changes nothing -> {revoked: [], ended_sessions: []}; remove_person {telegram_user_id} («Удалить человека» at the PC, a trust window: refused like delete_tree while untrusted sessions live or a request is Pending, {revoked: [], refused: window_unavailable}; refused {revoked: [], refused: owner} for the owner - a person bound as owner in the PC's bindings or with an active owner key on the PC; the owner has only «Удалить» per key) -> the person's keys with all their descendants go as by delete_tree, origin pc, the walk starting at the person's active keys and then tombstones (a tombstone keeps its origin), live sessions end, the person's attempts go and the grant token is replaced (every press; for a guest with only attempts on the PC the window calls it «Удалить попытки»); the bindings are untouched -> {revoked (walk order), ended_sessions}; attempt_allow / attempt_hide {telegram_user_id, key_id, role (allow only: the role the window showed)} (§10.2, at the PC, a trust window: {key_added: null, refused: window_unavailable} while unavailable; the role is never the server's word: owner for «владелец на этом ПК» - a person with an active owner key, or the owner by the PC's bindings - guest for anyone else; read at the press, a derived role other than the step's role writes nothing -> {key_added: null, refused: role} and the attempt stays (the agent reads it again at the write and cancels the press whole if it changed; the engine is synchronous); an owner's attempt, keys or none, needs a second explicit step - without second_step: true -> {key_added: null, second_step_required: true} and nothing changes; set {mode} (switching to strict ends every session whose verdict is not signed -> ended_sessions, reason key_unconfirmed for a session of an unconfirmed key, key_required for any other, then every Pending request, key_required); an account not in them is not added; null = no owner) -> sessions {session_id: role}; remote_input {session_id, target pairing_panel|pair_allow|strict_toggle|list_edit} -> {accepted}; pairing_panel {open}; confirm_window {open}; pair_request {..., viewer_key?} -> {viewer_key: accepted|ignored_no_panel|ignored_window_used|ignored_repeat|invalid|absent} (every request is kept by request_id with its person, with or without a key: «Разрешить» on it still binds the person; first wins: a repeat of a request_id still waiting - the server repeats waiting requests on reconnect - changes nothing, neither its person nor its key (or its lack of one), and answers absent / ignored_no_panel / ignored_window_used as usual, else ignored_repeat - a key in the repeat is not taken and does not spend the acceptance window, so a fresh request in the same opening still gets its key in); a press naming another role writes nothing -> {key_added: null, refused: role, journal: []}; a key that gets the derived owner role needs a second explicit step (without it {key_added: null, second_step_required: true, journal: []}); otherwise one press, and second_step is ignored; the same key active as the person's own record writes nothing and the record stays exactly as it is, its unconfirmed mark too (only confirm clears it) -> {key_added: null, already: works | waiting} (waiting: the record is unconfirmed; as the agent's KeyLanding::Already; the same for a pc_allow key at binding_added), except the owner's own guest-role record of that key, which is rewritten with the owner role, source pair, unless a strict-mode key_unconfirmed leaves the record as it was; with no owner at all the role is the one the step names; via pc_allow the role is always guest, and «владелец на этом ПК» is read at the press - then the key is not kept - and again at the activation, after binding_added is applied - then the kept key is forgotten, {key_added: null}: the owner gets no new guest key; binding_added {telegram_user_id, role?} (the person joins the bindings, role guest unless the step names one) (in strict mode a kept pc_allow key of the person is not activated and is forgotten, so a later binding_added finds nothing; a removal of the person - remove_person, binding_removed - does not touch the kept key: in observe a fresh one is written at a later binding_added, a removed one is not lifted) -> {key_added, role, unconfirmed}; confirm {key_id} (at the PC, one press - attempts recorded for the key's person do not change it; stays unconfirmed if a session other than a confirmed-owner signed one, or a Pending session request, existed since confirm_window opened) -> {unconfirmed}; delete_tree {key_id} (at the PC: key and its descendants via endorse.by/grant.by/invite.by; origin pc; the walk goes through inactive links: a revoked or replaced record keeps its edges and its descendants go too, while it stays revoked with its origin; a recover record inherits both the edges and the descendants of the records it replaced; every accepted press replaces the grant token, in either mode, for an owner key too and when the walk only goes through tombstones, and drops no attempt: it is no removal of the person) -> {revoked = only the keys this call revoked (active before it), as a set, ended_sessions [{session_id, verdict key_revoked}] = the live sessions of the deleted keys}, or, while any session other than a signed confirmed owner's is live or a session request is Pending (the trust window is unavailable, §10.1), {revoked: [], refused: window_unavailable} with no change (the token too). A recover commit likewise ends the live sessions of the replaced keys: offer expect ended_sessions (left out when none). An ended session is gone: reoffer -> {result: no_session}, remote_input -> {accepted: false}. reload: the PC restarts and reads its stored state back; live sessions, Pending requests, windows, rate limits and the nonce book (§2.2: in memory only) start afresh, so every nonce issued before the restart, spent or not, is nonce_unknown after it until a new nonce_batch. Ancestry edges are rebuilt from the records and the tombstones alone, so the store persists them in source (a tombstone keeps it): by (endorse, grant), invite_by (grant: only when the invite's signer differs from grant.by), parents (recover: the edges of the replaced records, deduplicated; may be absent when empty, and a reader treats absent as empty). expect.absent [field names] = fields the step's result must NOT carry, not even as a property set to undefined/null (every other expect field is compared one way: the result may carry more). state_after = key ids / revoked ids / spent ids after the step; when listed, also attempts [{telegram_user_id, key_id, count}] (a set) and unconfirmed (the ids of active keys marked unconfirmed) and roles ({key_id: role}, the stored role of each listed active key). sas_scenarios: one side's automaton; setup {add_id, req_id?, ...} after its rendezvous is open/joined (req_id: the tap that opened or joined it, already answered), or N's {join: true, req_id, ...} after its one address-less device_add_join {req_id} (§6.1), or O's {open: true, req_id, ...} after its one device_add_open {req_id}; req_id is that tap's (§6.1: fresh per tap): the joining N / opening O takes a server answer only with that req_id - another (a late answer to an earlier tap) or none is ignored; a device_add_closed whose req_id is not the current tap's is ignored in every state, after opened/joined too (a late not_found of an earlier tap never ends the running rendezvous), while a close of this add_id with no req_id ends it; once a tap is answered, nothing else answers it; a direct refusal of the current tap (its req_id, no add_id) is ignored when it is the known answer to the other request (none_waiting while opening, busy while joining), and any other reason, an unknown one too, ends the tap (ended <reason>) - after which an opened/joined with that req_id is ignored; N succeeds only on an endorse it received and accepted (done: true): device_add_closed done before one is ended done, no result; events recv <msg> | do send_commit | do send_key | do confirm | enter <6 digits> | server device_add_opened/joined/closed {add_id?, req_id?, reason?}; every setup names its side's own mode (O secret: {mode, add_id, s} takes only key; O sas: {mode, add_id, nonce_o} takes only commit/reveal; N secret: {mode, add_id, key_reg, s} sends key (on hello, or do send_key) and never a commit, reveal or SAS; N sas: {mode, add_id | join, key_reg, nonce_n}); a step of the other mode, or a received step that does not parse (a key_reg refused, a field not strict base64url) -> closed protocol; expect sent (+ mac for N's key) | sas | done | await sas_entry + tries_left (O never shows its own sas) | await confirm (secret: key_reg and mac checked) | closed <protocol|commit_failed|sas_failed> (the side closes it: device_add_close) | ended <reason> (the server closed it: device_add_closed of this rendezvous, or none_waiting with its req_id to the joining N, or busy with its req_id to the opening O - no automatic retry) | joined <add_id> (the joining N takes exactly one, with its req_id) | opened <add_id> (the opening O takes exactly one, with its req_id) | ignored (any other server event, and every event after the end: nothing is sent, opened or joined on its own). rendezvous_scenarios: the server's rendezvous (§6.1); sockets {name: account}; server_max_open (optional, a test parameter for the server's own bound on live rendezvous; absent = unbounded); events {from, send <device_add_open|join|send|resume|close>} or {from, disconnect: true} or {advance_ms} (the scenario's clock, from 0, no socket) -> expect [{to, msg}] in any order across recipients, in the listed order to one recipient, add_id r<n> = the n-th the server made, expires_at left out. Every open and join carries req_id; the server echoes it only in its direct answer to that socket: device_add_opened, the joiner's device_add_joined (the opener's has none), device_add_closed busy (open), none_waiting / not_found (join); an eviction's cancelled and a not_found to a send or resume carry none. Open with server_max_open: it fits unless live - (1 if the account already has 2 open, the place its eviction would free) >= server_max_open; a refused open gets busy {req_id} without add_id and evicts and makes nothing; an open that fits evicts (if the account has 2) and opens as usual. Join {add_id}: the account's open one nobody joined and another socket opened (one socket is never both sides), else not_found to the joiner. Join {}: the account's newest open role old + mode sas one nobody joined and another socket opened (secret never, its own never), else none_waiting without add_id. Open with 2 open in the account: the oldest closes with cancelled to its sides first. Resume {add_id, role}: a socket naming the other side gets role_mismatch without consuming the queue; the right side reattaches and receives its queue. A join while the opener's socket is disconnected sends device_add_joined to the joiner only; the opener's (no req_id) is owed and goes first on the opener side's resume, before its queue, once; if the rendezvous closes meanwhile, it is kept with the close and goes first with that side's kept steps, before the reason, under the same rules as the steps. Send into a rendezvous nobody joined yet closes it with protocol, to its opener (the first step goes only after device_add_joined); otherwise it relays to the other side, or queues while it is disconnected: at most ADD_QUEUE = 8 undelivered steps per side, and the 9th closes the rendezvous for both sides with protocol. Close: the other side gets device_add_closed with the reason. A closed rendezvous is gone (join and send get not_found), and its reason is kept for its account ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS = 120000 ms by the clock: a resume of its add_id meanwhile, from any socket of the account, gets device_add_closed {add_id, reason: <kept>} - never role_mismatch - preceded, in order, by the named side's undelivered steps when they are still kept: only to a socket that did not hold the other side at the close (that one gets only the reason), and only once (a later resume gets only the reason); at most ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MAX = 4 kept closes per account, a new one forgets the account's oldest; once that time has passed, once forgotten, or from another account, not_found. Besides ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MAX the server has a global bound on the volume of kept closes; a close forgotten under it answers not_found too (not stepped here). ADD_TTL_MS expiry is not stepped (scenarios stay well within it). Consumers assert both the verdict (expect) and `why` of every negative case: several cases are built so that a verifier missing one rule reaches a different verdict, and `why` names the rule that must refuse first.

scenarios.name: grant_after_removal_at_pc
scenarios.//: §7 «Смена», §10: C came in by g1. The person at the PC deletes C alone («Удалить», delete_tree): every removal press replaces the grant token. The spent g1 again is no ground on the removed key: key_revoked; g3 on the fresh invite i2, signed before the press (token ""), is grant_stale. Only a grant the owner signs after the press, over the new token, brings C back.

scenarios.//: §10.1, §7 «Смена»: B is Petya's guest key granted by A. scenarios.name: a_kept_pc_allow_key_removed_pc_is_not_lifted_by_binding_added_observe
scenarios.//: §5, §10: in observe mode Petya (a guest with his key C) asks again with C; «Разрешить» goes to the owner (pc_allow) and the PC keeps C for his BindingAdded. «Удалить человека» at the PC then removes Petya: C becomes a tombstone of origin pc, the token is replaced and his attempts go; the removal does not touch the kept key (residual §10). The server's binding_added that follows finds the kept C, but an unconfirmed «Разрешить» lifts no removal (the agent: removed): nothing is written and C stays removed with origin pc.

scenarios.name: a_kept_pc_allow_key_removed_by_the_server_is_not_lifted_by_binding_added_observe
scenarios.//: §5, §10, residual §10: as above, but the server removes Petya (binding_removed): C becomes a tombstone of origin server, the token is replaced; the kept key stays in memory. The binding_added that follows finds it, but an unconfirmed «Разрешить» lifts no removal of any origin: nothing is written and C stays removed with origin server.

scenarios.name: a_kept_fresh_pc_allow_key_is_written_after_a_removal_observe
scenarios.//: §5, residual §10: in observe mode Petya (a guest with his key C) asks with a fresh key X, never on the PC; pc_allow keeps X. «Удалить человека» removes Petya (C goes with origin pc, the token is replaced) and does not touch the kept X. The binding_added that follows writes X as Petya's unconfirmed guest key; C stays removed. Needs Petya's earlier press and the server's word; in observe he connects by the binding anyway, and «Подтвердить» at the PC is still needed for strict mode.

scenarios.name: a_fresh_pc_allow_key_after_a_removal_strict
scenarios.//: §5, residual §10: the same in strict mode: pc_allow keeps nothing, so after «Удалить человека» the binding_added writes nothing; C stays removed.

scenarios.name: allow_in_a_dirty_window_does_not_lift_a_removal_observe
scenarios.//: §5, §3.4: Petya's key C was removed at the PC (origin pc). He asks again with C; while the panel is open a session request (Pending) taints the window, so «Разрешить» in the panel would give an unconfirmed key, and an unconfirmed «Разрешить» lifts no removal (the agent: removed): nothing is written and C stays removed.

scenarios.name: allow_tainted_by_unsigned_session_during_window
scenarios.//: §3.4: a key accepted by Allow is confirmed only if no session other than a confirmed-owner signed one existed from opening the panel to the click.

scenarios.name: fresh_grant_with_the_current_token_admits_at_once
scenarios.//: §7 «Токен выдачи», §10: the server removed Petya at pc_clock_at_0_ms + 10000 and that removal gave the PC its current grant token (initial grant_token). The owner's fresh grant on a fresh invite carries that token: it was signed after the removal, so it admits Petya's new device C at once - no 1 h wait, and its issued_at (pc_clock_at_0_ms + 1000, before the removal on the owner's clock) does not matter. The admission keeps the token. The old g1 (token ""), never spent, stays grant_stale.

scenarios.name: removed_person_first_use_and_server_word_observe
scenarios.//: §10, §9, residual risk: Petya is in the snapshot, has no key, and the server removed him (binding_removed: he leaves the binding list, the token is replaced). A keyless removal leaves no removed key, so in observe mode his first_use admits an unconfirmed key (the snapshot is never cut), and the server's word (pc_allow, then BindingAdded) adds another unconfirmed guest key. Strict mode admits neither: an unconfirmed key is not admitted there, and «Подтвердить» is a press at the PC.

scenarios.name: pc_removal_after_server_removal_replaces_the_token
scenarios.//: §10: the server removes Petya (his key C goes, origin server); then the PC removes him («Удалить человека»): the walk goes through C's tombstone, which keeps its origin. §7 «Смена»: the first removal replaces the grant token (C goes, the binding goes), and so does the press at the PC (every removal press does, even one that only walks through tombstones); a later server removal changes nothing for Petya (no key, no binding), writes nothing and keeps the token. A grant signed before the removals (token "") is grant_stale; «Разрешить» at the PC brings Petya back with a new device in one press.

scenarios.//: §10: Petya's key Y was deleted at the PC (tombstone pc). His phone C signs a new endorse for Y; while the PC checks that endorse's signature, the person at the PC deletes C (during_ground_verify). The PC re-reads the signer's record: the signer is gone, so the endorse is no ground; on a removed key that is key_revoked, nothing written or spent, Y's tombstone stays.

Petya never connects, and the owner removes him once more: the removal takes him off the binding list, so it replaces the token. g2, given between the two removals, is grant_stale.

scenarios.name: binding_removed_of_a_guest_drops_the_guests_attempts
scenarios.//: §10, §10.2: a person's removal by the server's word is the same step as «Удалить человека» at the PC: the token is replaced and the person's attempts go. Petya (a bound guest with no key) has an attempt with key Z, 703 (a bound guest) one with key X. 702 has only a key removed at the PC and no binding: binding_removed of 702 takes no guest key and no binding, so it changes nothing (the token stays). binding_removed of Petya takes his binding: the token is replaced and his attempt goes; 703's stays.

scenarios.name: store_with_an_unspent_ground_is_damaged

scenarios.name: store_with_a_tombstone_without_removed_at_is_damaged
scenarios.//: §10: every tombstone carries removed_at, when it was written (unix ms on the PC's clock); the time rule for a returning endorse reads it. A store whose tombstone lacks it is damaged: the agent refuses to read it (expect_initial: key_list_damaged, read_failed, why removed_at).

rendezvous_scenarios.//: The socket that opened a sas rendezvous is not attached to it by its own address-less join: it gets another waiting one, or none_waiting.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: queue_holds_8_undelivered_steps
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: each side's queue holds at most ADD_QUEUE = 8 undelivered steps; the 9th closes the rendezvous for both sides with protocol, and it is gone: the away side's resume within ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS gets its kept steps in order, then the kept reason, protocol.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: queue_9th_undelivered_step_closes_protocol
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: each side's queue holds at most ADD_QUEUE = 8 undelivered steps; the 9th closes the rendezvous for both sides with protocol, and it is gone: the away side's resume within ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS gets its kept steps in order, then the kept reason, protocol.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: busy_at_the_server_bound_opens_nothing
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: the server does not open a rendezvous beyond its own bound on live ones (server_max_open, a test parameter here): busy with the open's req_id and no add_id, and no rendezvous is made (the next one is still r2). A join is not refused for the bound; a freed place opens again.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: at_the_server_bound_an_eviction_makes_room
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: whether an open fits counts the place the eviction of the account's oldest would free. Bound 2, the account has 2 open: its third open evicts the oldest (cancelled to its sides) and opens, not busy; another account's open is still busy and evicts nothing.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: resume_after_the_close_tells_the_kept_reason
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1 ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS: N's socket was away when O closed. Within 120 s a resume of r1 from any socket of the account gets the kept reason: from O, which held the other side (no role_mismatch), naming either side, and from N's new socket. Another account's resume gets not_found.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: queued_endorse_delivered_before_done_on_resume
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: N's socket was away while the person typed the digits; O sent endorse (queued for N) and closed with done. Within ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS: O's socket (it held the other side) naming new gets only done, the endorse stays kept; another account gets not_found; N's resume gets the endorse first, then device_add_closed done (N succeeds on the endorse it accepts, never on done alone); the queue goes once, so a later resume naming new gets only done.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: kept_closes_capped_per_account
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1 ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MAX = 4 kept closes per account: five rendezvous close in turn, the fifth forgets the first. A resume of the first gets not_found, of the fifth its kept reason.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: kept_close_reason_lasts_120_s
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1 ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS = 120000 by the scenario clock ({advance_ms}): 1 ms before it the resume still hears the kept reason; once it has passed, not_found.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: a_step_before_the_join_closes_protocol
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: the first step goes only after device_add_joined; a step into a rendezvous nobody joined closes it with protocol (to its opener, the sender), and it is gone.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: join_by_add_id_never_from_the_opener_socket
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: a device_add_join {add_id} from the socket that opened that rendezvous gets not_found (with its req_id), as an address-less one never attaches it; the rendezvous stays open for another socket.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: opener_away_at_join_resume_gets_joined_then_steps
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1 «Должное отсутствующей стороне»: O's socket is away when N joins, so O's device_add_joined is owed (N gets its own at once). N's step waits in O's queue. O's resume gets the owed joined first (the opener's copy: no req_id), then the step; later steps go live.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: opener_away_at_join_kept_close_gives_joined_steps_then_closed
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: O's socket is away when N joins and N sends a step; then N closes while O is still away. Within ADD_CLOSED_KEEP_MS (119999 ms later) O's resume from a fresh socket gets, in order, the owed device_add_joined, the kept step, then the close; the owed joined goes with the queue, once — a later resume gets only the reason.

rendezvous_scenarios.name: owed_joined_never_to_the_socket_that_held_the_other_side
rendezvous_scenarios.//: §6.1: O's socket is away when N joins; N sends a step and closes. N's socket — the one that held the other (new) side at the close — resumes naming the opener's side (old): it gets only the reason, neither the owed device_add_joined nor O's step. O's page, from a fresh socket, then still gets the owed joined, the step, then the close.
